tasks.title: All customers
tasks.statement: Output all columns and all rows of the customers table. The star * means "all columns".
tasks.hint: SELECT * FROM customers;

tasks.title: All products
tasks.statement: Output the entire contents of the products table.
tasks.hint: Replace ... with the table name.

tasks.title: One column
tasks.statement: Output only the product names: the title column of the products table.
tasks.hint: Instead of *, list the column you need: SELECT title FROM products;

tasks.title: Two columns
tasks.statement: Output the name and city of every customer (the name and city columns of the customers table).
tasks.hint: Columns are listed separated by commas.

tasks.title: Column order
tasks.statement: Output the customer columns in reverse order: city first, then name.
tasks.hint: The order of columns in the result is the order in the list after SELECT.

tasks.title: Three columns
tasks.statement: From products, output three columns: title, category, price, in exactly this order.

tasks.title: Column alias
tasks.statement: Output the product name under the name product (an alias is set with the word AS): a product column, from the products table.
tasks.hint: SELECT title AS product FROM products;

tasks.title: Alias with a space
tasks.statement: Output city under the header `Город` (aliases with spaces or non-Latin letters are put in double quotes) for the customers table.
tasks.hint: AS "Город": the name in double quotes.

tasks.title: Arithmetic without a table
tasks.statement: SELECT works without FROM too. Calculate 2 + 3 * 4 and output it under the name result.
tasks.hint: Multiplication runs before addition: the result is 14.

tasks.title: Parentheses
tasks.statement: Calculate (2 + 3) * 4 under the name result.
tasks.hint: Parentheses change the order of operations.

tasks.title: Five operations
tasks.statement: In one row, output the results of 10 + 5, 10 - 5, 10 * 5, 10 / 5, 10 % 3 under the names plus, minus, mult, div, rest.
tasks.hint: % is the remainder of division.

tasks.title: Integer division
tasks.statement: Output 7 / 2 as div_int and 7 / 2.0 as div_real. Note that dividing integers throws away the fractional part.
tasks.hint: If at least one number is fractional, the result is fractional.

tasks.title: String literal
tasks.statement: Output the string `'привет'` (in single quotes) in a column greeting.
tasks.hint: Strings in SQL go in single quotes: `'привет'`.

tasks.title: Apostrophe in a string
tasks.statement: Output the string O'Brien in a column name. An apostrophe inside a string is written twice.
tasks.hint: 'O''Brien'

tasks.title: Boolean values
tasks.statement: Output the results of the comparisons 1 = 1 and 1 = 2 under the names yes and no. In SQLite, true is 1 and false is 0.

tasks.title: Value types
tasks.statement: Output the types of values with the function typeof: for 1, 1.5, 'a' and NULL under the names a, b, c, d.
tasks.hint: typeof(expression) returns integer, real, text or null.

tasks.title: Computed column
tasks.statement: From the products table, output title and the price with a 10% discount (price * 9 / 10) under the name sale_price.
tasks.hint: Arithmetic works right in the column list.

tasks.title: Value of the stock
tasks.statement: For each product, output title and the value of the stock on hand (price * stock) as stock_value.

tasks.title: Joining strings
tasks.statement: Output one string per product of the form `Название (Категория)`, that is, title, a space, and the category in parentheses: use the || operator for concatenation; column label.
tasks.hint: title || ' (' || category || ')'

tasks.title: A tag in every row
tasks.statement: Output the customer's name and the constant `'клиент'` in a column kind.
tasks.hint: A constant can be output as a column.

tasks.title: Division remainder
tasks.statement: For each product, output title and the remainder of dividing stock by 10 (column rest).

tasks.title: Dividing the price
tasks.statement: Output title and price / 100 (the integer part) as hundreds.
tasks.hint: Both numbers are integers, so the fractional part is thrown away.

tasks.title: No repeats: cities
tasks.statement: Output the list of customer cities without repeats (DISTINCT): column city.
tasks.hint: SELECT DISTINCT city FROM customers;

tasks.title: No repeats: categories
tasks.statement: Output the product categories without repeats.

tasks.title: No repeats: statuses
tasks.statement: Output all the distinct order statuses (the orders table).

tasks.title: Distinct pairs
tasks.statement: Output the distinct pairs (category, brand) from products.
tasks.hint: DISTINCT applies to the whole result row at once.

tasks.title: Table.column
tasks.statement: Output the customers' name, giving the column together with the table name: customers.name.
tasks.hint: A column name can be qualified with the table name and a dot.

tasks.title: Table alias
tasks.statement: Output the name and city of customers, giving the table the alias c (FROM customers AS c) and referring to the columns as c.name, c.city.
tasks.hint: FROM customers AS c

tasks.title: Tables of the database
tasks.statement: The database stores its own descriptions in the system table sqlite_master. Output the names of all tables in the database (type = 'table') in alphabetical order: column name.
tasks.hint: SELECT name FROM sqlite_master WHERE type = 'table' ORDER BY name;

tasks.title: How many tables
tasks.statement: How many tables are in the database? Output the number under the name n.
tasks.hint: COUNT(*) counts rows.

tasks.title: Table columns
tasks.statement: Output the column names of the orders table in the order they were declared: SELECT name FROM pragma_table_info('orders') ORDER BY cid;
tasks.hint: pragma_table_info('table') describes the columns.

tasks.title: Primary key
tasks.statement: Which columns make up the primary key of the order_items table? Output their names (pk > 0) in order of pk.
tasks.hint: In pragma_table_info the key columns have pk > 0.

tasks.title: Foreign keys
tasks.statement: Output the foreign keys of the orders table: the columns "from", "table" and "to" of the function pragma_foreign_key_list('orders').
tasks.hint: The words from, table, to are keywords, so they go in double quotes.

tasks.title: Row count
tasks.statement: How many rows are in the customers table? Output the number as n.

tasks.title: Departments
tasks.statement: HR database. Output the name and city of all departments (the departments table).

tasks.title: Employees and salary
tasks.statement: HR database. Output the name and salary of every employee.

tasks.title: Annual salary
tasks.statement: HR database. Output the name and the annual pay (salary * 12) as per_year.

tasks.title: Courses
tasks.statement: School database. Output the title and hours of all courses.

tasks.title: Classes without repeats
tasks.statement: School database. Output the students' classes (class) without repeats.

tasks.title: Films
tasks.statement: Films database. Output title and year for all films.

tasks.title: Directors' countries
tasks.statement: Films database. Output the directors' countries without repeats.
